style: Art for a 2D top-down fantasy role-playing game. Bright, colorful medieval fantasy in clear daylight. Realistic proportions, nothing cartoonish, nothing grim. No text, no borders, no watermarks, no drop shadows.

sections.name: Dungeon material textures
sections.brief: Four different flat seamless material swatches for an overhead fantasy RPG, on a 1024 by 1024 sheet arranged in a precise 2 by 2 grid. Each square quadrant is its own complete uninterrupted edge-to-edge opaque texture. Hard cuts exactly at the row and column midlines, with no dividing strip or blending between quadrants. First two quadrants are overhead floor patterns and the fourth is an overhead environmental hazard. Bottom left is a wall-face texture seen straight from the front, with small horizontal masonry courses and no top or bottom trim. Even soft light, small details distributed throughout the frame, no horizon, architecture, staging, perspective, central object or gradients. Match opposite edges within each square, especially along the horizontal edge of the wall face. Detailed hand-painted pixel texture, quiet contrast so hero and loot sprites are clear at small screen sizes. Palette and materials in grid order: {item}
items: Top left: blue grey water-worn harbour flagstone pavers with subtle oyster lime and teal undertones. Top right: old honey-brown parallel dock planks with small nail heads. Bottom left: cool grey cellar limestone blockwork with scattered damp teal seams. Bottom right: muted blue teal harbour water with small calm ripples and gently glinting surface.

Top left: muted moss green slate flagstones with soft rounded edges. Top right: alternating old russet timber planks of a sluice walkway. Bottom left: mossy olive grey limestone courses. Bottom right: cool green reservoir water with diffuse duckweed and sparse light ripples.

Top left: weathered ochre sandstone flagstones in uneven ashlar pattern. Top right: worn sandy terracotta terraced floor tiles. Bottom left: gold and rust-toned sandstone blocks in shallow horizontal courses. Bottom right: loose dry earth with ochre grains and small slate fragments.

Top left: russet packed loam with a subtle close net of tiny roots. Top right: patches of muted olive mulch and grey pebbles. Bottom left: horizontal natural layers of brown earth and worn rock crossed by small buried roots. Bottom right: ivory spider silk strands over bark brown earth, low contrast and randomly scattered.

Top left: desaturated charcoal basalt flagstones with tiny green grey mineral details. Top right: dappled rusty copper forge grating in a uniform tight grid. Bottom left: cool black volcanic masonry with rubbed warm brown edges. Bottom right: burnt orange molten rock with small glowing veins between dark crusts.

Top left: blue violet slate with subdued specks of grey quartz. Top right: indigo polished stone tiles with frosted mauve highlights along the edges. Bottom left: muted lilac-grey rock bedding with sparse saturated blue crystal chips embedded into the bedrock. Bottom right: deep cobalt mineral pool with small rippling turquoise silver highlights.

Top left: cool pale grey square stone flagstones with worn frost along some edges. Top right: textured pale blue hard-packed snow with evenly distributed icy flecks. Bottom left: slate grey cut stone courses with pale blue frozen mortar. Bottom right: muted clear azure glacier ice with fine natural fracture lines.

Top left: pale cream marble flagstones with delicate honey veins and soft edges. Top right: medium warm walnut herringbone parquet, aged. Bottom left: warm white marble ashlar with occasional bronze pins at widely spaced intervals. Bottom right: dark blue black ink ripples with muted pewter surface reflections.

sections.name: Dungeon landmarks and fixtures
sections.brief: Sixteen separate hand-painted medieval fantasy map props in a precise 4x4 grid with four exact rows and four exact columns. One prop per cell, with ample transparent air gaps and each entire silhouette well within its cell, minimum 22 pixels clear margins on all four sides. Match only the reference's material detail and camera angle, not the depicted subjects or row count. About 35 degrees raised from above and slightly in front, soft upper-left light, consistent painted pixel look and life-size proportions. Large readable silhouettes. No ground, no shadow, no grass, nothing behind the character or object. No glow, haze or backdrop. Real transparent alpha behind every object. No symbols resembling written letters, captions, numbering, outlines or visible grid. Read the sixteen pieces row by row: {item}
items: Row 1, dock cellar: upright brass bilge pump and hand lever on a compact iron stand; rugged oak pallet with two bound cargo casks; short rough wooden table with an unmarked closed ledger and a copper quill; neat spool of thick hemp rope. Row 2, moss sluice: upright brass-and-wood handwheel on a narrow mossy iron stand; squat stone pedestal with a bronze carp statue; stone lectern with a blank ivory tablet; wooden marsh lantern on a low post. Row 3, sandstone burial hall: heavy upright round sandstone seal disc fitted in a square carved stone frame; ochre sandstone sarcophagus with a compact chamfered lid; sandstone votive plinth with a bronze brazier bowl; squat terracotta grave jar. Row 4, root tunnels: upright wood lever lashed to a narrow knotted root stand; upright cluster of capped amber mushrooms on a single short exposed stump; small knot of ivory silk on a wooden rack with an unmarked carved stone tablet in the middle; curled knot of three dried root tendrils.

Row 1, basalt forge: big copper valve wheel on a squat black stone stand; small basalt forge hearth with orange coals contained inside the firebox; blacksmith tongs and a copper tablet on a compact wrought iron stand; short copper and basalt coal bucket. Row 2, crystal grotto: small blue quartz prism held by a brass pivot gimbal atop a stone pedestal; cluster of short brilliant violet and blue quartz points on a compact rocky base; slate lectern holding an amber crystal lens; small naturally faceted lavender quartz cluster. Row 3, ice hall: upright pale blue ice barrier set into a narrow iron frame with a brass clasp; compact frozen stone fountain with thick icy rim; small grey stone altar with an unmarked silver medallion and short blue candles; pale blue ice stalagmite cluster. Row 4, marble archives: upright walnut index mechanism with a bronze lever and one visible gear; walnut shelving case with old bound volumes and brass corners; marble lectern holding a blank open velum book; short open walnut document chest with a few rolled blank papers inside.

Sixteen CLOSED dungeon barriers, never standalone controls. All are self-contained gates without surrounding architecture, floor or scenery. Camera stays fixed through the whole sheet. Row 1 in exact order, wide front-facing silhouettes roughly twice as wide as tall: grey wrought iron floodgate with broad squared bars and dark teal ironwork; heavy striped timber sluice gate with green iron hinges; golden sandstone burial gate with a central carved round stone seal disc in wide square stone frame; dense brown rootwork and opaque ivory spider silk closing a low bark arch. Row 2 in exact order, wide front-facing silhouettes roughly twice as wide as tall: dark iron forge vent shutter with short copper bands and louvres; violet quartz barrier with dark slate posts and a solid row of amethyst points; opaque pale blue ice barrier with iron edges and a brass clasp; polished brass archive grille with square diagonal lattice and walnut lower bar. Row 3 in exact order, actual perpendicular narrow side views of the same four barriers from row 1: sideways iron floodgate; sideways wood sluice gate; sideways sandstone burial seal; sideways root-and-silk barrier. Row 4 in exact order, actual perpendicular narrow side views of the same barriers from row 2: sideways iron vent shutter; sideways violet quartz barrier; sideways opaque ice barrier; sideways brass archive grille. For rows 3 and 4, the barriers run north to south along the vertical axis of the image, seen from above and very slightly off the right side, each reading considerably taller than it is wide. Keep their silhouettes materially distinctive, and paint their top and narrow right face so they read in a left-to-right corridor. All sixteen are separated by the specified empty margins.

sections.name: Dungeon creature sprites
sections.brief: Exactly four separate full-body fantasy creature sprites in a strict 2 by 2 grid, one each in top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right. Each centered in its cell and at least 32 pixels clear from all cell edges. For all four use the same slightly raised camera, three-quarter side view facing screen left, in a natural braced pose with full bodies, feet and weapons visible. Use the reference for brush detail and camera only. Match a bright detailed hand-painted pixel look, soft light from upper left, realistic material and adult human proportions where relevant. Readable contrasting silhouettes, no gore or heavy outlines. No ground, no shadow, no grass, nothing behind the character or object. No glow, haze or backdrop. Genuinely transparent background and empty margins. The four in order: {item}
items: Top left: Bilge Scavenger, a short agile ratlike dock goblin with warm russet fur, narrow muzzle, patched harness and a short brass hook. Top right: Barnacle Guard, a full-height drowned human sailor in sea-green mail and a barnacle-encrusted cuirass, round weathered brass shield and short sword. Bottom left: Sluice Stalker, a lean quadrupedal olive amphibian with webbed feet and a narrow crocodilian head, yellow-green reed frills along its upper back. Bottom right: Reed Hexer, a tall pale swamp humanoid caster wearing muted sage ragged robes with reed braids, carrying a long knotted staff with a small blue stone mounted at the head.

Top left: Barrow Soldier, a towering skeleton in sand-worn bronze armour, carrying a dark bronze straight short sword and round shield. Top right: Grave Tender, a gaunt adult guardian in an ochre linen burial robe and faded violet sash with a long urn-topped staff. Bottom left: Root Crawler, a thick-bodied mottled hardwood centipede with a low arched segmented body and dark copper limbs, small flecks of moss. Bottom right: Silk Widow, a large grey brown spider with eight long jointed legs and pale cream markings, front body slightly raised.

Top left: Furnace Hound, a muscular black-brown mastiff with copper collar, subtle burnt orange cracks in basalt plates on the shoulders, paws on the same level. Top right: Slag Binder, a hooded adult humanoid forge custodian in russet leather and basalt armor holding copper tongs and an orange coal orb held between their tips. Bottom left: Shardling, a squat agile creature formed from cobalt-blue crystals with small smoky grey joints, broad limbs. Bottom right: Crystal Seer, an upright faceted amethyst golem with pale quartz shoulders and long translucent blue quartz staff.

Top left: Rime Wolf, a silver-white winter wolf with dense realistic fur and dark grey paws, braced and head low. Top right: Icebound Guard, a tall adult human warrior in tarnished ice-blue plate and indigo wool with a pale steel axe and weathered iron shield. Bottom left: Index Automaton, a human-height walnut and bronze clockwork construct with a small circular brass head, compact broad shoulders, stepped brass joints and a bronze polearm. Bottom right: Ink Familiar, a small crouching black ink creature with an elongated corvid head, dark purple feathers and two grasping forelimbs.
